title: Example 13-2: Poem with One Level

illustrates.quote: The indention pattern is based on the entire poem. The main entry begins in cell 1. Each subentry level begins two cells to the right of the previous level. All runovers begin two cells to the right of the farthest indented level. One level: 1-3 Two levels: 1-5, 3-5 Three levels: 1-7, 3-7, 5-7 Four levels: 1-9, 3-9, 5-9, 7-9 etc.

blocks.features: Untitled excerpt (opening lines of Walt Whitman's "Song of Myself"); ordinary body-text font, left-aligned in print, one level of poetic line with no sub-indention.

lines.text: My tongue, every atom of my blood, form’d from this soil, this air,
Born here of parents born here from parents the same, and their parents the same,
I, now thirty-seven years old in perfect health begin,
Hoping to cease not till death.

print.notes: Picture on PDF p.357; four lines, each fitting on one print line with no visual indention among them (a genuine one-level poem, matching the example's title).
